overlap.title: A written law is entrusted for custody and periodic public reading
overlap.summary: The narrative attributes law writing to Moses and directs custody beside the ark and a seven-year public reading.
overlap.reasoning: A narrative attribution to Moses is evidence of the authorship claim made within the book, rather than external verification of the surviving book’s complete composition. The closing narrator’s perspective must be distinguished from the earlier law-writing attribution; this distinction alone does not identify an author, editor or date.
overlap.scope: This does not identify the deposited manuscript, establish its survival or show how regularly the reading occurred.

checks.overlapDecision: Reviewed existing overlapping findings and all six ENTRIES studies; subject differs, no duplicate finding.

overlap.title: Celestial lights and the creation sequence
overlap.summary: Read as a physical creation sequence, this passage places the Sun after Earth’s vegetation, conflicting with the scientific account. Calling stars “lights” is not itself an error.
overlap.reasoning: A literal sequence placing terrestrial vegetation before the Sun conflicts with the solar-system formation model. The issue is the sequence, rather than describing luminous objects as lights.
overlap.scope: This assessment applies to a literal first-creation chronology. A literary or theological reading does not necessarily make the same scientific claim. Reading this as the later visibility of already-existing lights also changes the claim being evaluated; NASA does not establish that interpretation.

checks.overlapDecision: Distinct allotment-purpose Q, not a repeat of the creation sequence finding; reasonable light/time and national-worship readings retained without treating either as established.

overlap.title: The military census is not a count of everyone
overlap.summary: The 603,550 total counts eligible males from age twenty and excludes the Levites.
overlap.reasoning: Internal agreement of these totals does not independently verify the ancient population. Treating the number as the size of the whole traveling community overlooks the census criteria.
overlap.scope: The population scale, Hebrew numerical terminology, chronology and archaeological evidence need separate investigation. No demographic multiplier or historical certification is supplied here.

overlap.title: Levi’s blessing differs from Jacob’s rebuke
overlap.summary: Genesis rebukes Simeon and Levi together; Deuteronomy gives Levi a positive priestly blessing and no separate blessing named for Simeon.
overlap.reasoning: The tribal portraits differ, but praise for a later role does not logically deny earlier wrongdoing. The two speeches also have different speakers and narrative occasions.
overlap.scope: The omission is a feature of this blessing’s list, not proof that Simeon ceased to exist or a secure date for the poem. Historical explanations need further evidence.

checks.overlapDecision: Published deuteronomy-levi-blessing-and-rebuke notes Simeon’s omission in a comparison about Levi. This Q examines the material unexplained omission itself with alternatives, not another finding of conflict or disappearance.
